description: The Global Drillhole Database is a compilation of more than 3.95 million drillholes, boreholes, mineral occurrences and rock samples from public geological survey databases, with identifiers, coordinates, depths, drilling year, target commodities and a link to each source record. By region it holds about 3.02 million records from Western Australia, 379,000 from Canada, 262,000 from South Africa, 200,000 from South Australia, 60,000 from Greenland and 38,000 from Tasmania. It was compiled by a Hugging Face user, kcribb12, from agencies such as the Western Australian mines department, Canadian provincial surveys, South Africa's Council for Geoscience and GEUS in Greenland. The 1.21 GB dataset is free as Parquet and JSON files under CC BY 4.0, with the licences of the source surveys also applying. Caveats: it is an individual's compilation without documented validation, fields are harmonised across very different sources, and coverage is limited to six regions. For simulation it offers a single table of subsurface observation points for mineral supply studies, geological models and ground condition screening along planned infrastructure in those regions. It is related to the Western Australia mineral exploration drillholes and Nova Scotia Drillhole Database records in this catalogue, two of the kinds of sources it combines.
